issues.description: New AWS client created per inbound context frame — connection churn under load
issues.detail: Every LLMContextFrame opens a fresh `async with self._aws_session.client('bedrock-agentcore', ...)` and tears it down when the response finishes. For a streaming voice pipeline this means a new TCP/TLS handshake and signing context per turn. The client should be created once (e.g., lazily on first use or in a startup hook) and reused; otherwise this is the kind of patch that looks fine in a demo and falls over the first time it ships to a real workload.

issues.description: `agentArn` parameter violates the codebase's naming convention
issues.detail: Python is snake_case. The surrounding code is snake_case. There is no reason for `agentArn` to be camelCase except that it matches the boto3 key. Every other AWS-flavored field on the same constructor (`aws_access_key`, `aws_region`, etc.) is snake_case. Match the existing style: rename to `agent_arn`. This is exactly the kind of thing that wastes the next maintainer's time and shows up forever in grep.

issues.description: Unhandled `json.JSONDecodeError` in default response transformer will kill the stream
issues.detail: `default_response_to_output_transformer` calls `json.loads(response_line)` with no try/except. A single malformed SSE line — which happens — raises and propagates out through `process_frame`, leaving `self._output_response_open=True` and a dangling `_close_task`. At minimum, catch the decode error, log, and return None. Bonus: the unmatched `LLMFullResponseStartFrame`/`EndFrame` bookkeeping is fragile to any exception in this whole block; wrap the invoke in try/finally that always closes the response.

issues.description: Class name in module docstring disagrees with the actual class name
issues.detail: Module docstring says `AWSAgentCoreProcessor`, the PR title says `AWSBedrockAgentCoreProcessor`, and the class is `AWSAgentCoreProcessor`. Pick one. The discrepancy between PR title and code suggests this was renamed mid-review without a sweep. Decide on the name (the title's `AWSBedrockAgentCoreProcessor` is more searchable and aligns with the AWS product naming) and make code + docstring + commit message agree.

issues.description: `from .agent_core import *` with no `__all__` exports everything including loguru/aioboto3
issues.detail: The module has no `__all__`, so the star-import re-exports `asyncio`, `json`, `os`, `aioboto3`, `logger`, every imported frame class, plus the two transformer helpers. This is how namespaces rot. Either define `__all__ = ['AWSAgentCoreProcessor', 'default_context_to_payload_transformer', 'default_response_to_output_transformer']`, or import the symbols explicitly in `__init__.py` instead of star-importing. The surrounding `__init__.py` already does `from .llm import *` and `from .nova_sonic import *`, so look at how those modules constrain exports and match that.

issues.description: `isinstance(last_message, LLMSpecificMessage)` then calls `.get(...)` on it in the same expression
issues.detail: In `default_context_to_payload_transformer`: `if isinstance(last_message, LLMSpecificMessage) or last_message.get('role') not in ('user', 'system')`. Short-circuit evaluation saves you here, but the intent is muddy and the next person reading this has to think about it. Split into two clauses, or convert to early-returns. Also: silently dropping `LLMSpecificMessage` and assistant messages with no log line means a misconfigured caller gets a silent no-op, which is the worst failure mode.

issues.description: Output-response bookkeeping race between the 1s timeout task and the post-loop close
issues.detail: `_close_output_response_after_timeout` reads/writes `_output_response_open` and pushes `LLMFullResponseEndFrame` without coordinating with the main `process_frame` path. If the timeout fires while `process_frame` is between iterations, you can close the response, then the next text frame opens a new one mid-stream — splitting a single agent turn into multiple bookended responses. Either guard with a lock, or drop the timeout entirely and rely on the explicit close after the response loop. The timeout exists to handle delayed-final-chunk cases; if you keep it, document the race and the invariant.

issues.description: SSE parsing is hand-rolled and brittle
issues.detail: Splitting on `\n` and slicing `line[6:]` reinvents SSE parsing badly. It will mis-handle CRLF, comment lines starting with `:`, multi-line `data:` fields, and event boundaries. Either use a real SSE parser (httpx-sse, aiohttp-sse-client) or document that this only handles the trivial `data: <json>\n` shape that AgentCore happens to emit today and will break the moment AWS changes the wire format. Magic number `6` should at minimum be `len('data: ')` with a comment.

`self._last_text_frame_time` is assigned in `_push_text_frame` and never consumed anywhere. Dead state. Delete it, or use it (e.g., for the timeout decision instead of cancel/recreate). Also `get_event_loop()` is deprecated in newer Python when there's no running loop; prefer `asyncio.get_running_loop()` if you do need it.

issues.description: Branch on `LLMSpecificMessage`/role uses dict-style `.get` on a typed object
issues.detail: Calling `.get('role')` works for dict messages but `LLMSpecificMessage` is presumably a class. The isinstance check guards it via short-circuit, but the pattern leaks duck-typing in a place where the types diverge. A small helper `_get_role(msg) -> Optional[str]` would be obvious and testable.

Two pure functions (`default_context_to_payload_transformer`, `default_response_to_output_transformer`) and a stateful frame processor with non-trivial bookend logic and zero unit tests. The pure transformers especially are free to test — string in, string out. Land those at minimum. The processor's timeout/close logic is the kind of code that grows bugs in production silently; cover the happy path and the timeout race.

issues.description: Default region fallback to `us-east-1` hidden inside a getenv default
issues.detail: `aws_region or os.getenv('AWS_REGION', 'us-east-1')` silently picks us-east-1 if nothing is set. That's a footgun for non-US users who think they configured their region and didn't. Either log the region selection on init, or refuse to default and require an explicit region. At minimum mention it in the docstring.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The shape of the patch is fine — frame processor in, AgentCore invocation out, text frames result — but the implementation has the smell of a first cut that hasn't been run against real load. The two biggest sins: opening a fresh boto3 client per turn (handshake cost on every utterance in a voice pipeline) and `agentArn` in camelCase in a snake_case codebase. The unhandled `json.loads` in the default response transformer will eventually crash mid-stream and strand the response-open bookkeeping. The hand-rolled SSE parser, the dead `_last_text_frame_time`, and the racy timeout-close vs. final-close bookkeeping all suggest the streaming path needs another pass. Land it after: rename `agentArn` to `agent_arn`, reuse the client across calls, wrap the default response transformer and the invoke loop in proper error handling so bookends always close, constrain `__all__`, and add at least the two transformer unit tests. Reconcile the PR title vs. class name vs. module docstring while you're at it.
